chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah the Exalted said in His Book: 'So whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [from which he must cut hair] shall offer a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice.'

So whoever is afflicted with an ailment or pain and uses what is not permissible for the Muhrim (one in Ihram) when he is healthy, then [the expiation is]: fasting for three days, or charity to ten poor people by feeding them until they are satisfied, or a sacrifice (Nusk) of a sheep which he slaughters, eats from, and feeds from; and he is only required to perform one of these.

And there is no contradiction between this narration and the one that preceded it regarding the quantity of feeding, because the first narration states that he feeds six poor people, two Mudds for each poor person, and the last narration states ten poor people, for each of them an amount that satisfies them; and he is free to choose either of the two reports, and it is valid for him.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Muhrim who cuts their hair or uses perfume due to illness?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to detail the specific expiations (Kaffarah) for unintentional violations of Ihram restrictions, such as cutting hair or using perfume, citing the Quranic verse 2:196. The text resolves apparent discrepancies in other narrations regarding the quantity of food (feeding six people two Mudds each versus feeding ten people a full meal) by establishing them as valid alternative options for the Muhrim to choose from, reflecting the Shia scholarly approach to reconciling hadith reports.
